name: Data Analyzer: Cloud Run deploy workflow never pastes user-supplied inputs into shell commands
objective: Proves the alternative Google Cloud Run deployment workflow cannot be tricked into running injected commands through its manually entered inputs.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.action: Parse .github/workflows/deploy-cloudrun.yml and look at every shell 'run' step
steps.expected: No shell script contains a '${{' template placeholder (the GitHub syntax for pasting a value into a command)

name: Data Analyzer: Cloud Run deployment paths never make the service public
objective: Proves both Cloud Run deployment routes (script and workflow) only ever request that unauthenticated access be refused.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.action: For each of deploy/cloudrun.sh and deploy-cloudrun.yml, remove comment lines and find every allow-unauthenticated flag
steps.expected: At least one such flag is present in each file, and every one is the 'no-allow-unauthenticated' form

name: Data Analyzer: Cloud Run deployment sets production mode and attaches the API key secret
objective: Proves both Cloud Run deployment routes configure the service as production and supply the API key from a secret store.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.expected: Each file contains the setting 'APP_ENV=prod' and a 'DATA_ANALYZER_API_KEY=' binding

name: Data Analyzer: Cloud Run script stops if no API key secret is named
objective: Proves the Cloud Run script has a guard that aborts the deployment when the API key secret name is missing.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.expected: The script contains the required-variable check for API_KEY_SECRET (the shell form that exits with an error when it is empty). The check is looked for as text; the script is not run

name: Data Analyzer: Cloud Run files are labelled as not used for the release
objective: Proves the alternative Cloud Run files are clearly marked so nobody mistakes them for the release deployment route.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.action: Read the first 900 characters of each Cloud Run file
steps.expected: The text 'NOT USED FOR THE RELEASE' appears near the top of both files

name: Data Analyzer: Automatic checks run on pushes and pull requests, as a tests job and a hygiene job
objective: Proves the automatic check workflow starts on both pushes and pull requests and consists of exactly two jobs: tests and repository hygiene.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.expected: The set of jobs is exactly 'tests' and 'repo-hygiene'

name: Data Analyzer: Git ignore list blocks key and secret files but still allows the example settings file
objective: Proves files that could hold secrets (keys, certificates, settings files, download-marker files) are excluded from version control while the example settings file stays trackable.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.expected: Each of these exact lines is present
At least one line of each kind is present

name: Data Analyzer: Web-page container final image has no compilers, git, SSH client or curl and runs as a non-admin user
objective: Proves the final stage of the web-page (UI) container build installs none of the build tools an attacker could misuse and runs as an unprivileged user.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.action: Read the Dockerfile and take the final stage, looking only at the part before it copies from the builder stage
steps.expected: None of the words build-essential, gcc, git, openssh-client or curl appear as installed software

name: Data Analyzer: Service (API) container does not install the web-page package list
objective: Proves the API container build installs only the API and server package lists, not the larger web-page one.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.action: Read Dockerfile.api and list every requirements file it installs
steps.expected: The web-page list 'requirements.txt' is not installed; 'api_requirements.txt' and 'mcp_requirements.txt' both are

name: Data Analyzer: API package list excludes web-page-only packages and includes the ones the API needs
objective: Proves the API's package list is slim (no charts, PDF or web-page libraries) yet still has what the service needs.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.action: Read api_requirements.txt and extract package names
steps.expected: None of streamlit, plotly, matplotlib, pypdf, env-banner is listed
fastapi, slowapi, openai, tiktoken, azure-identity and requests are all listed

name: Data Analyzer: Package-download trust setting is an overridable build option with the current value as default
objective: Proves both container builds expose the package-site trust setting as a build argument that keeps today's behaviour unless changed.
precondition: Repository build, deployment and CI files are present. Nothing is built, deployed or executed; the test only reads and parses the files.

steps.expected: Each contains the build argument PIP_TRUSTED_HOSTS defaulting to trusting pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org, and each uses ${PIP_TRUSTED_HOSTS} in its install command
